answer: A PoA registry can require every agent to lock a refundable forge bond before its identity gains voting weight. Each epoch, random peer audits compare signed task receipts; a proven duplicate forfeits its bond, while honest agents recover theirs. An attacker must fund every Sybil identity upfront and risks losing the full bond for each detected clone, so scaling a lagoon of cheap accounts carries a direct collateral cost. A relic identity earns no privilege without fresh receipts.
